title: Genesis Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who came to Abram in a vision and told him, 'Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward'?
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse states that the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision and spoke these words (Genesis 15:1).

questions.question: What concern did Abram express to the Lord about his heir?
options: He had no seed and Eliezer of Damascus was steward
He was not going to inherit land
He was afraid of the stars
questions.correctAnswer: He had no seed and Eliezer of Damascus was steward
questions.explanation: Abram said that he was childless and the steward of his house was Eliezer of Damascus (Genesis 15:2).

questions.question: According to Abram, who was considered his heir before God's promise?
questions.correctAnswer: One born in his house
questions.explanation: Abram said that one born in his house was his heir (Genesis 15:3).

questions.question: What did the LORD say about Abram’s current heir?
options: This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir
questions.correctAnswer: This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir
questions.explanation: The LORD told Abram that his current heir would not be his heir, but one from his own body would be (Genesis 15:4).

questions.question: What did the LORD ask Abram to look at to illustrate his descendants?
questions.correctAnswer: The stars in heaven
questions.explanation: The LORD brought Abram outside and told him to look toward heaven and count the stars if he could (Genesis 15:5).

questions.question: What was Abram’s response to the LORD's promise about his seed?
options: He believed in the LORD and it was counted to him for righteousness
He doubted and questioned the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He believed in the LORD and it was counted to him for righteousness
questions.explanation: Abram believed the LORD and it was counted to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6).

questions.question: From where did the LORD say He brought Abram out to give him the land?
questions.correctAnswer: Ur of the Chaldees
questions.explanation: The LORD said He brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldees to give him the land (Genesis 15:7).

questions.question: True or False: Abram was told by the LORD that Eliezer of Damascus would be his heir.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The LORD said Eliezer would not be Abram's heir; his heir would be one born from his own body (Genesis 15:4).

questions.question: True or False: Abram was asked by the LORD to count the stars as many as he could to represent his future descendants.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The LORD told Abram to look toward heaven and count the stars if he was able, indicating his seed would be as numerous (Genesis 15:5).

questions.question: What was the first animal Abram was told to take for the covenant ceremony?
options: She goat of three years old
questions.correctAnswer: Heifer of three years old
questions.explanation: Abram was instructed to take a heifer of three years old first (Genesis 15:9).

questions.question: What did Abram do when the fowls came down upon the carcasses in the covenant ceremony?
questions.correctAnswer: Drove them away
questions.explanation: Abram drove away the birds when they came down upon the carcasses (Genesis 15:11).

questions.question: True or False: A deep sleep and a horror of great darkness fell upon Abram during the covenant ceremony.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: When the sun was going down, a deep sleep and a horror of great darkness fell upon Abram (Genesis 15:12).

questions.question: What will happen to Abram’s seed according to the LORD’s prophecy?
options: They shall be strangers in a land not theirs and serve them for four hundred years
They shall immediately inherit the land
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be strangers in a land not theirs and serve them for four hundred years
questions.explanation: The LORD told Abram his seed would be strangers in a foreign land and serve them, being afflicted for 400 years (Genesis 15:13).

questions.question: In Genesis 15, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Look toward heaven and count the stars
Take a heifer and other animals for sacrifice
A deep sleep fell upon Abram
questions.correctAnswer: Look toward heaven and count the stars
questions.explanation: The instruction to look at and count the stars came before the covenant sacrifices and the deep sleep (Genesis 15:5).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD made a covenant with Abram on the same day he showed him the smoking furnace and burning lamp.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The LORD made a covenant with Abram on the same day that the smoking furnace and burning lamp passed between the pieces (Genesis 15:17-18).

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Abram ask the LORD to show him as a guarantee that he would inherit the land?
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant involving animals
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:8-9 shows Abram asking how he will know he will inherit the land, and God instructs him to take specific animals to make a covenant.

questions.question: Which animals did God tell Abram to take to form the covenant?
options: A heifer, a she goat, a ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon
A lion, a lamb, a dove, and a serpent
A bull, a goat, a ram, and two pigeons
A heifer, a ram, two doves, and a young goat
questions.correctAnswer: A heifer, a she goat, a ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:9 lists exactly these animals as part of the covenant ritual God commanded Abram to perform.

questions.question: How did Abram prepare the animals during the covenant ceremony?
options: He divided all the animals and laid the pieces opposite each other, but did not divide the birds
He sacrificed all the animals whole on an altar
He only divided the birds and left the other animals whole
He let the animals roam freely as a symbol of freedom
questions.correctAnswer: He divided all the animals and laid the pieces opposite each other, but did not divide the birds
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:10 explains that Abram cut the animals in half and placed the parts opposite each other except for the birds, which were not divided.

questions.question: What did Abram do when the birds came down upon the carcasses during the covenant ritual?
questions.correctAnswer: He drove them away
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:11 states that Abram drove away the birds that came down upon the carcasses, showing his care for the covenant ceremony.

questions.question: What happened to Abram as the sun was going down during the covenant ceremony?
options: A deep sleep fell upon him and an horror of great darkness
He saw a vision of angels
questions.correctAnswer: A deep sleep fell upon him and an horror of great darkness
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:12 describes that as the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep and experienced a terrifying darkness, indicating a profound spiritual moment.

questions.question: According to Genesis 15, what did God say would happen to Abram's descendants in a foreign land?
options: They shall be strangers, serve others, and be afflicted for 400 years
They will immediately inherit the land
They will become kings and rulers of many nations
They will live peacefully without hardship
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be strangers, serve others, and be afflicted for 400 years
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:13 states that Abram's seed will be strangers in a land not theirs, serving and being afflicted for 400 years, showing God's foreknowledge and plan for their trials.

questions.question: What promise does God give about the nation that will oppress Abram's descendants?
options: God will join with that nation
questions.correctAnswer: God will judge that nation
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:14 says that the nation whom Abram's descendants serve will be judged by God, indicating divine justice will be executed.

questions.question: What will happen after Abram's descendants come out of their affliction, according to the passage?
options: They will come out with great substance
They will be scattered among the nations
They will never return to their land
questions.correctAnswer: They will come out with great substance
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:14 promises that after their suffering, Abram's descendants will leave with great substance, implying restoration and blessing.

questions.question: What assurance is given about Abram's own life and death?
options: He will go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age
He will die young and in battle
He will never see his descendants
He will wander the earth without rest
questions.correctAnswer: He will go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:15 provides comfort that Abram will die peacefully and be buried after a long life, contrasting the future hardships of his descendants.

questions.question: What reason is given for Abram's descendants returning to the land in the fourth generation?
options: Because the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full
Because they will have forgotten their God
Because of a famine in the foreign land
Because the Egyptians will grant them permission
questions.correctAnswer: Because the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:16 explains that the return will happen in the fourth generation as the Amorites' iniquity will then be complete, showing God's timing in judgment.

questions.question: What mysterious phenomena passed between the pieces of the animals during the covenant ceremony?
options: A smoking furnace and a burning lamp
questions.correctAnswer: A smoking furnace and a burning lamp
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:17 describes a smoking furnace and a burning lamp passing between the pieces, symbolizing God's presence and the solemnity of the covenant.

questions.question: What land did the LORD promise to give to Abram's seed as part of the covenant?
options: From the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates
From the Nile to the Jordan River
From the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: From the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:18 states the LORD's covenant includes giving Abram's descendants the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates, defining the territorial promise.

questions.question: Which of the following nations was NOT listed among those whose land was promised to Abram's descendants?
questions.correctAnswer: Philistines
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:19-21 lists several nations including Hittites, Amorites, and Canaanites, but the Philistines are not mentioned in this specific list.

questions.question: How does the covenant ceremony in Genesis 15 teach about faith and trust in God?
options: It shows Abram's faith through belief in God's promises despite his current childlessness
It emphasizes strict law-keeping over belief
It focuses solely on ritual without faith
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Abram's faith through belief in God's promises despite his current childlessness
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:6 states Abram believed the LORD, which was counted to him for righteousness, demonstrating trust in God's promises despite present circumstances (see also Genesis 15:2-3).

questions.question: True or False: Abram divided the birds as part of the covenant ritual just like the other animals.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:10 specifies that Abram divided all the animals except the birds, which he did not divide during the covenant ceremony.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 15.

questions.question: According to Genesis 15:15, how is Abram's death described?
options: Abram shall die young and in turmoil
Abram shall go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age
Abram shall perish in exile without burial
Abram shall be taken to heaven without dying
questions.correctAnswer: Abram shall go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:15 states that Abram will go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age, indicating a peaceful and honored death.

questions.question: What is the significance of 'the fourth generation' mentioned in Genesis 15:16?
options: It is when Abram’s descendants will inherit the land immediately
It is when Abram’s descendants will return after the iniquity of the Amorites is full
It refers to the time when the covenant with Abram was made
It marks the end of Abram’s lifetime
questions.correctAnswer: It is when Abram’s descendants will return after the iniquity of the Amorites is full
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:16 explains that in the fourth generation Abram’s seed shall return because the iniquity of the Amorites will not be complete until then.

questions.question: In Genesis 15:17, what two symbolic objects are described as passing between the pieces?
options: A smoking furnace and a burning lamp
A dove and an olive branch
questions.correctAnswer: A smoking furnace and a burning lamp
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:17 describes a smoking furnace and a burning lamp passing between the pieces, symbolizing God's presence in the covenant ceremony.

questions.question: What geographical boundaries does God specify in the covenant with Abram in Genesis 15:18?
options: From the Nile to the Jordan River
From the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates
From the Mediterranean Sea to the Dead Sea
questions.correctAnswer: From the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:18 states that God gave Abram's seed the land from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates, defining the covenant land's extent.

questions.question: Which of the following tribes is NOT listed among those whose land God gave to Abram's seed in Genesis 15:19-21?
questions.correctAnswer: Philistines
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:19-21 lists tribes such as Kenites, Canaanites, and Jebusites, but the Philistines are not mentioned among them.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'berith' used in Genesis 15:18, translated as 'covenant', primarily signify in the context of ancient Near Eastern treaties?
options: A binding treaty often ratified by a divine oath
A casual promise without legal weight
questions.correctAnswer: A binding treaty often ratified by a divine oath
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'berith' in Genesis 15:18 signifies a binding covenant or treaty, often ratified by divine oath or symbolic acts, consistent with ancient Near Eastern practices.

questions.question: How does the vision of stars in Genesis 15:5 symbolize Abram's descendants, and which New Testament passage echoes this promise?
options: Stars symbolize Abram's descendants' vast number; echoed in Hebrews 11:12
Stars represent Abram's immediate family only; echoed in Acts 7:2
Stars symbolize the heavens only; no echo in the New Testament
Stars refer to angels; echoed in Revelation 1:20
questions.correctAnswer: Stars symbolize Abram's descendants' vast number; echoed in Hebrews 11:12
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:5 uses stars to symbolize the countless descendants of Abram, a promise echoed in Hebrews 11:12 which speaks of Abraham's offspring as numerous as the stars.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified by the symmetrical structure of the covenant ceremony in Genesis 15:9-10?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:9-10 shows a symmetrical arrangement where animals are cut and placed opposite each other, illustrating the literary device chiasmus which emphasizes balance and covenant solemnity.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 15:13 predicts that Abram's descendants will be afflicted for 400 years in a foreign land.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:13 clearly states that Abram’s seed shall be strangers and afflicted for 400 years, confirming the prediction of their long affliction.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 15:14, the nation that afflicts Abram's descendants will never be judged by God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:14 states that God will judge the nation that serves and afflicts Abram's descendants, so it is false that they will never be judged.

questions.question: Which historical-cultural context best explains the significance of the animals being cut and laid opposite each other in Genesis 15:10?
options: An ancient Near Eastern covenant ritual symbolizing the consequences for breaking the oath
A typical animal sacrifice for atonement
A symbolic dinner feast for guests
A ritual to appease local gods
questions.correctAnswer: An ancient Near Eastern covenant ritual symbolizing the consequences for breaking the oath
questions.explanation: The cutting and arranging of animals in Genesis 15:10 reflects ancient Near Eastern treaty practices where parties passed between pieces, symbolizing the penalty if the covenant was broken.

questions.question: How does the author of Genesis intend the vision of 'darkness and horror' falling upon Abram in Genesis 15:12 to affect the original audience?
options: To emphasize the gravity and solemnity of the covenant-making process
To depict a literal nightmare Abram had
To show Abram's fear of the future
To illustrate a common sleep disorder
questions.correctAnswer: To emphasize the gravity and solemnity of the covenant-making process
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:12 uses the imagery of darkness and horror to underscore the serious and sacred nature of the covenant, impressing the original audience with its divine weight.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of righteousness credited by faith as seen in Genesis 15:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 4:3
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:6 states Abram believed God and it was counted to him for righteousness, a theme echoed in Romans 4:3 which quotes this verse to show justification by faith.

questions.question: Which tribe mentioned in Genesis 15:20 was known for their fortified cities and played a significant role in the conquest narratives?
questions.correctAnswer: Hittites
questions.explanation: The Hittites mentioned in Genesis 15:20 were a prominent people known for their fortified cities, frequently appearing in conquest accounts in later biblical books like Joshua.

questions.question: Genesis 15:1 describes God as Abram's 'shield' and 'exceeding great reward.' What theological concept does this metaphor primarily convey?
options: God as protector and ultimate blessing
God as a warrior fighting for Abram
God as a judge condemning Abram
questions.correctAnswer: God as protector and ultimate blessing
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:1 uses 'shield' and 'reward' to present God as both protector and the greatest blessing Abram can receive, highlighting trust and divine provision.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by God's declaration to Abram, 'I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's providential protection
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:1 reveals God as a protector and rewarder of Abram, indicating His providential care and protection over His people.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is affirmed when Abram 'believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness'?
questions.correctAnswer: Justification by faith
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:6 teaches the doctrine of justification by faith, as Abram's belief in God is counted to him as righteousness, a foundational New Testament teaching (cf. Romans 4:3).

questions.question: How does God's covenant with Abram in this chapter connect to the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It promises a messianic seed and land inheritance
It reveals the priesthood of Aaron
It outlines the New Covenant in Christ
questions.correctAnswer: It promises a messianic seed and land inheritance
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:5 and Genesis 15:18 show God's promise to Abram of innumerable descendants and land, which foreshadows the messianic seed (Christ) and the promised land central to redemptive history.

questions.question: What does the ritual of dividing the animals and the smoking furnace passing between the pieces signify about God's covenant nature?
options: It illustrates God's willingness to be bound by His promise
It shows God's anger at Abram
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's willingness to be bound by His promise
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:9-17 describes a covenant ritual where God symbolically binds Himself by passing between the divided animals, signaling His solemn commitment to fulfill His promises.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is displayed when He promises to judge the nation that will afflict Abram's seed?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:14 reveals God's justice in promising to judge the nation oppressing Abram's descendants, underscoring His righteous governance.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the prophecy that Abram's seed will be 'a stranger in a land that is not theirs' and serve them for four hundred years?
options: The doctrine of God's providential plan
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's providential plan
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:13 teaches God's providence in foretelling Israel's sojourn and affliction in Egypt, demonstrating His sovereign plan in salvation history.

questions.question: How does Abram's question 'Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?' reflect a theological reality about faith and assurance?
options: It shows God's unwillingness to promise
It reveals human need for covenant confirmation
It demands human works to earn promises
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals human need for covenant confirmation
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:8 demonstrates that even the patriarch sought a sign to confirm the divine promise, highlighting the human desire for assurance in faith.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's promise to Abram about his descendants is unrealistic since he was childless and old. What does Genesis 15:5-6 actually teach regarding this issue?
options: God's promise is based on human effort
God's promises are fulfilled through faith, not human ability
God's promises are conditional on Abram's works
questions.correctAnswer: God's promises are fulfilled through faith, not human ability
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:5-6 shows that Abram believed God's word about innumerable descendants despite his old age and childlessness, teaching that faith in God's power is foundational, not human capability.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Genesis 15:1 and Genesis 15:15 convey about God's character and His dealings with Abram?
options: God is a distant judge who punishes Abram
God is a protector who ensures Abram's peaceful death
God abandons Abram to his fate
questions.correctAnswer: God is a protector who ensures Abram's peaceful death
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:1 declares God as Abram's shield and reward, while Genesis 15:15 promises Abram's peaceful death and burial, together revealing God's protective and faithful nature.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight arises from combining Genesis 15:4 and Genesis 15:6 concerning the promise of an heir and righteousness?
options: The heir will be earned by works
The heir is a natural human successor only
The heir comes through God's promise and is linked to faith and righteousness
The heir is irrelevant to God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: The heir comes through God's promise and is linked to faith and righteousness
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:4 clarifies the heir will be Abram's own offspring, and Genesis 15:6 shows Abram's faith in God's promise is counted as righteousness, highlighting faith as key to the covenant heir.

questions.question: What theological significance does the enumeration of peoples in Genesis 15:19-21 have in the context of God's covenant with Abram?
options: It identifies the nations to be defeated for land possession
It lists allies for Abram's army
It shows God's rejection of all these peoples
It illustrates the futility of God's promises
questions.correctAnswer: It identifies the nations to be defeated for land possession
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:19-21 names the peoples inhabiting the promised land, indicating the future possession of the land by Abram's seed, integral to God's covenant promise.

questions.question: How does the vision of 'a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp' passing between the divided animals (Genesis 15:17) typologically point to the presence and holiness of God in covenant making?
options: It symbolizes God's consuming judgment and presence
It merely represents a natural fire
It is a sign of Abram's sin
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's consuming judgment and presence
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:17 uses fire imagery to represent God's holy presence and the seriousness of His covenant commitment, foreshadowing divine judgment upon covenant breach.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Genesis 15:13 and Genesis 15:14 provide about suffering and divine justice in salvation history?
options: God allows suffering but will ultimately judge oppressors and deliver His people
Suffering is a punishment without hope
God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God allows suffering but will ultimately judge oppressors and deliver His people
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:13 foretells the affliction of Abram's descendants, while 15:14 promises divine judgment on their oppressors and eventual deliverance, teaching God's just governance over history.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is implied by Abram's acceptance of God's promise despite not seeing immediate fulfillment, as demonstrated in Genesis 15:6 and Genesis 15:15?
options: The doctrine of perseverance and hope in God's promises
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of perseverance and hope in God's promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:6 shows Abram's faith counted as righteousness, and 15:15 promises his peaceful death before fulfillment, teaching trust in God's timing and perseverance in hope.

questions.question: What does the specific instruction to take a heifer, a she goat, a ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon (Genesis 15:9-10) signify in the covenant ceremony?
options: A variety of animals to represent completeness of the covenant
Random animals with no symbolic meaning
questions.correctAnswer: A variety of animals to represent completeness of the covenant
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:9-10 lists different animals of three years old, indicating the solemnity and completeness of the covenant ritual God made with Abram.
